title: Actionable exception patterns and language-specific examples for SDKs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Define concrete, actionable exception surface and example patterns across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs so application authors get deterministic retry guidance, ergonomic streaming behavior, and clear telemetry. This ticket produces: (1) canonical error codes and short textual codes, (2) language-specific exception/type patterns and migration guidance, (3) recommended retry semantics per error class, (4) streaming error shapes and reconnection/resume recipe, (5) example snippets for each language and (6) a rollout plan (feature flags + deprecation window).

Motivation: Customers are experiencing inconsistent retry behavior across SDKs and unclear streaming error handling. SREs see unnecessary retries for non-idempotent requests; product teams want actionable user messages rather than generic 500s. This reduces customer support load and improves app reliability.

Non-goals: Changing runtime error codes or behavior; this ticket only maps and surfaces errors consistently in SDKs. Runtime will follow up for any code changes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDKs expose a documented error taxonomy (code + message + retriable bool + suggested action) and language bindings exist for Python/TS/Go. 2) Retry behavior implemented in SDKs respects retriable flag by default with exponential backoff and jitter and is configurable. 3) Streaming client surfaces a StreamError event with resume token when available; reconnection example works end-to-end in tests. 4) Integration tests added to each SDK exercise at least RateLimit, TransientNetwork, ModelError, and StreamClosed scenarios. 5) Docs page + migration snippet merged and linked from top-level SDK README.
design_decision_summary: Adopt hybrid error model: stable string 'code' (eg. 'rate_limit_exceeded') + numeric 'http_status' for correlation. SDKs will expose typed errors (Python classes, TS error.code enum, Go sentinel errors + helper funcs). Each error includes 'retriable' and an optional 'action' field with concise guidance. Streaming errors will include 'resume_token' when runtime provides it; otherwise expose idempotency guidance. Telemetry will standardize on tags: error.code, sdk.name, sdk.version, request_id, attempt_count, latency_ms, model, route. We will not change server-side codes in this ticket; mapping layer inside SDKs will normalize variants.
implementation_notes: Create a small language-agnostic JSON file (errorset) in runtime repo listing canonical codes, short descriptions, retriable flag, and suggested client action — SDKs consume this during release cycles.

Python: Provide base class RedwoodError(Exception) with subclasses RateLimitError, TransientError, ValidationError, ModelGenerationError, StreamClosedError. Add .code and .retriable attributes and .action_hint string. Update client to raise these instead of generic HTTPError.

TypeScript: Export a RedwoodError class extending Error with 'code' (string literal union) and 'retriable' boolean. Provide isRetriable(err) helper and typed guards for stream errors. Preserve Error.captureStackTrace compatibility.

Go: Define package errors with type Error struct { Code string; Msg string; Retriable bool } and sentinel values (var ErrRateLimit = Error{Code: \"rate_limit_exceeded\", Retriable: true}). Provide errors.Is/As helpers to interop with stdlib errors.

Retries: default policy = exponential backoff with full jitter, base=200ms, max_delay=10s, max_attempts=5. For rate limits, honor Retry-After header where present and treat Retry-After as stronger signal (max_attempts can be extended by config).

Streaming ergonomics: client exposes async iterator (TS/Python) and channel/iterator (Go). On transient stream errors, SDK will surface an error event with optional resume_token. Provide example wrapper util that automatically attempts resume when resume_token present and user opts-in. Do NOT auto-resume by default to avoid unexpected duplication unless request is idempotent or user sets resume=true.
Telemetry: all errors logged with structured fields and a short human message. Add SDK-level counters for error.code and histograms for retry attempts per request.
Testing: add fault-injection tests that return 429 with/without Retry-After and streaming mid-chunk disconnects; assert SDK maps to correct error types and adheres to retry config.
Docs & Examples: write migration snippets for existing users showing how to catch new typed exceptions and how to implement backoff in app code.
work_breakdown: ENG: create canonical errorset and publish schema (runtime) — 2d
ENG: implement Python types + tests + docs — 3d
ENG: implement TypeScript types + tests + docs — 3d
ENG: implement Go types + tests + docs — 3d
DOCS: examples page + changelog entries + migration guide — 2d

updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff meeting with SDK leads (Maya, Lars, Priya). Agreed canonical fields: code, message, retriable, action_hint, resume_token (stream-only).

2025-02-14: Draft of canonical errorset created in runtime repo (link below). Included 18 codes (rate_limit_exceeded, transient_network_error, model_internal_error, invalid_request, unauthorized, stream_closed, quota_exceeded, unsupported_model). Requested review from runtime team.
2025-02-18: Design review feedback: prefer stable string codes rather than numeric-only. Added 'action_hint' for user-facing suggestions. Runtime team confirmed no code renaming in this cycle.
2025-02-22: Python PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/421 — implements RedwoodError base and mapping table. Initial tests for 429 mapping added. Assigned to Priya for review.

2025-02-25: TS PR prototyped for error.code union and isRetriable helper. Noted one API ergonomics concern: capturing stack + preserving .cause across transpilation targets. Follow-up: ensure source maps and preserve stack messages.
2025-02-27: Decided not to auto-resume streaming by default due to duplication risk. Added opt-in resume API: stream.resume_from(token) and client helper auto_resume=true opt-in.
2025-03-01: Updated acceptance criteria to require integration tests and docs. Preparing release branch for sdks-2025.03.
2025-03-01: Blockers: need runtime team to publish final errorset v1.0 by 2025-03-05 to avoid SDK code drift. Open dependency logged below.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Auto-retries could cause duplicate side-effects for non-idempotent endpoints. Mitigation: default to not retry non-idempotent requests; expose clear config and guidance in action_hint. Risk: Stream resume may not always be supported by runtime. Mitigation: SDK will detect absence of resume_token and fall back to throwing StreamClosedError with action_hint to re-send idempotent request or use conversation ID for server-side deduplication.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Release Python 1.8.0-beta and TS 2.5.0-beta to 5% of installs behind feature-flag 'new-error-surface' for 2 weeks
Phase 2: Monitor errors by code and consumer feedback, increase to 25% for another week. Verify SLOs and support tickets decrease for common cases.
Phase 3: Default enable for all SDKs in sdks-2025.03 and announce deprecation for legacy error mapping in 60 days.
qa_plan: Add unit tests for mapping table, integration tests that simulate 429 and transient TCP disconnects. For streaming, add harness that simulates mid-stream disconnects and validate resume_token behavior and user-level error shapes. Validate telemetry tags emitted in local test telemetry backend. QA to run canary and confirm no increase in failed requests to runtime.
notes_for_review: Reviewers: focus on the language ergonomics (idiomatic Python/TS/Go patterns), the default retry policy parameters, and the streaming resume opt-in shape. Pay special attention to user-facing action_hint wording — these will appear in logs and support tickets. Confirm telemetry fields are sufficient for SRE triage (request_id, attempt_count, error.code).
